related_resources.reason: Monte Carlo construction and variance-reduction theory

authorship.scope: Original worked probability and Monte Carlo foundation lecture with mathematical companion; prior manuscripts preserved.

prerequisites.reason: Integration as an expectation and estimation from uniform samples.
Joint probabilities and how covariance affects sampling error.

recommended.reason: Optional deeper treatment of laws of large numbers, concentration and normal approximation.

background: Arithmetic, fractions, basic functions, and elementary probability; simple integrals for Monte Carlo lectures. No measure theory required.
readiness_checks: Derive the antithetic-pair estimator for the integral of x squared.
Calculate importance weights and explain their necessity.
Distinguish unbiasedness from having finite sampling variance.

description: Compares antithetic variates, control variates, stratification, and importance sampling as methods for reducing Monte Carlo error without merely increasing sample count.
